correctness.rationale: In a synchronous one-generation infectious process seeded at a root on a tree, infection passes along each unique root path precisely when its Bernoulli edges are open. Thus the earliest maximum generation count and cumulative infections at that generation are exactly computable for each percolated rooted tree. Independent recursive unlabeled-rooted-tree generation by multisets of subtrees (not the package Prüfer-code method) produced counts (1,1,2,4,9,20,48), 85 rooted types for n<=7. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 2^(n−1) edge-open masks within each type and exact conditional Bernstein differences found no negative differences for n<=6, and exactly the two claimed seven-vertex polynomials 7H_A=1+2p²+5p⁵−5p⁶ (last Bernstein difference -1/6) and 7H_B=1+6p²+6p³−23p⁴+25p⁵−11p⁶ (last difference -1/2). These complete finite enumerations provide exhaustive proof of the natural n<=7 cutoff; derivative-transform/Descartes argument yields a single interior maximum for each exception. The package certificate is consistent with the independent computation.

originality.rationale: Ozbay–Nielsen–Nguyen established nonmonotone peak-indexed cumulative epidemic burden by Monte Carlo on larger networks; the exact rooted single-seed tree problem and minimum-size seven-vertex threshold are not treated in its inspected primary results. Exact continuous-time SIR tree equations concern expectations of instantaneous compartments, not the path-dependent earliest-peak statistic. The new finite complete cutoff and explicit two polynomial laws are not a corollary of the prior numerical phenomenon. This is qualified because search cannot exclude all other combinatorial epidemic-tree enumerations.
residual_risks: Result is specific to one-generation infection duration, single root seed, first attainment of maximum prevalence and rooted tree topologies; changing tie convention changes the object.
Complete enumeration is only n<=7; it proves sharp onset, not a classification or frequency for larger trees.
Older exact tree-epidemic results outside searched materials could contain equivalent small-case examples; originality remains best-of-knowledge.

value.rationale: The motivating epidemic paradox asks how expected cumulative infection burden at its peak can decrease with higher edge transmissibility. Finding the exact first rooted-tree size at which the phenomenon is possible and classifying all minimal exceptions is a natural complete finite structural obstruction, with exact two polynomials and a sharp six/seven boundary. Exhaustive finite classification is a valid proof for this finite cutoff and does not purport to solve larger graphs.
